Change the garden-edge patch near the CENTRE of the image, ABOVE the chicken run and to the UPPER-LEFT of the house, into a recognisable productive FOOD FOREST: varied-height generic broad-canopy trees, smaller trees, shrubs and dense low leafy ground cover growing together in a layered managed patch, irregular mulched access path running through it, visible open access to plants. Photorealistic agricultural documentary, matching morning light and realistic plant texture. This remains an imaginary teaching scene, not a planting recommendation.

Visible upright stems, long arching leaves and some tassels, still believable at this aerial scale and in morning light. Leave narrow unplanted field-edge access and existing paths. No claims about spacing, yield, irrigation or season.
Add a modest rustic livestock KRAAL on an open field-edge patch at the LEFT side, just ABOVE the main vegetable garden, approximately x=70..310, y=320..475 in this 1672x941 composition. A simple oval or irregular timber-post and pole enclosure with a clear closed gate, dry earth floor, containing one believable cow and two goats at natural scale. The animals must read as a cow and goats, not horses or tiny chickens. A little basic shade at one edge if needed, but no new home. Keep enclosure outside vegetable beds and clear of the kitchen garden; don't draw livestock free-ranging through crops. This is a visual example, not a recommended enclosure specification or stocking recommendation.
Preserve every other feature and location, especially the central layered food forest and the fruit-bearing trees. Do not remove fruit or flatten the understory. No additional species labels, no text, numbers, dimensions, coloured zones or graphics. No luxury estate. Edge-to-edge photographic realism.
